findings.claim: ADR-0016 detects a subagent call by `agent_type`. In Claude Code 2.1.283 `agent_type` is also set on the MAIN thread of a session started with --agent. Only `agent_id` marks a subagent. v2 will treat the main thread of every --agent session as a subagent and apply case B/C rewrites there.
findings.evidence: strings of /opt/homebrew/Caskroom/claude-code@latest/2.1.283/claude: agent_id: "Subagent identifier. Present only when the hook fires from within a subagent ... Absent for the main thread, even in --agent sessions. Use this field (not agent_type) to distinguish subagent calls from main-thread calls." agent_type: "Present when the hook fires from within a subagent (alongside agent_id), or on the main thread of a session started with --agent". v1 hooks/pretooluse.mjs:167 `input.agent_id != null || input.agent_type != null`.
findings.archaeology: INTRODUCED_BY: 85f64d2c 2026-06-21 fix(hooks): respect subagent ctx tool availability (#834, fixes #794/#832). ORIGINAL_INTENT: 'subagent-originated WebFetch/curl/inline-HTTP/build redirects now pass through instead of forcing blocking ctx_* calls'. REGRESSION_RISK: v1 already has the same --agent false positive; v2 copies it and now rewrites instead of only skipping. SAFE_FIX_CONSTRAINTS: keep #794 behaviour for real subagents; key detection on agent_id only, use agent_type only to look up the tool set.
findings.fix: ADR-0016 'How the subagent's tools are known': subagent = `agent_id` present; `agent_type` only selects the tool row. Add a GP3 golden: main thread of `claude --agent x` carries agent_type without agent_id -> main-session path.

findings.claim: The tool-set lookup reads only `.claude/agents/<type>.md` (project, user) and only the `tools:` key. Claude Code agents can also come from plugins and from `--agents` JSON, and the frontmatter has `disallowedTools` and `mcpServers`. A subagent with `disallowedTools: mcp__*` or no ctx server is classed as case A (ctx tools) and gets a deny it cannot follow: the #794 dead end comes back.
findings.evidence: CC 2.1.283 binary agent frontmatter key list: ["name","description","prompt","tools","disallowedTools","model","effort","permissionMode","mcpServers","hooks","maxTurns","skills",...]. ADR-0016:19 'No `tools:` line means the agent inherits all tools, MCP included.'
findings.archaeology: v1 never parsed agent files: 85f64d2c sets mcpToolsAvailable = !isSubagentContext for every subagent (hooks/pretooluse.mjs:171). The per-type lookup is new in v2, so the #794 fix is at risk only through this new path.
findings.fix: Define the tool set as tools minus disallowedTools, with ctx tools present only if the context-mode server is in scope (mcpServers / inherited). Sources: project, user, plugin agents dir, --agents JSON. An agent type not found in any source -> case B/C, never case A. Add goldens for disallowedTools and plugin agents.

findings.claim: Case C says `updatedToolOutput` works for 'all tools'. In CC 2.1.283 MCP tools use a separate field `updatedMCPToolOutput`. A replacement that fails the tool's output schema is dropped and the ORIGINAL output goes to the model (logged only). PostToolUse hooks run in parallel on the original output and the last write wins, so another plugin's hook can overwrite ours. Each of these paths lets the full output into the subagent context: this breaks the ADR-0016 MUST.
findings.evidence: CC 2.1.283 binary: updatedToolOutput 'Replaces the tool output before it is sent to the model'; updatedMCPToolOutput 'Replaces the output for MCP tools only'; 'PostToolUse hook returned updatedToolOutput that does not match ${tool}'s output shape' then `_r=oo.data` (original kept); 'hooks run in parallel on the ORIGINAL output, so an identity rewrite competes last-write-wins with sibling rewrites'.
findings.archaeology: No v1 precedent: git log -S updatedToolOutput in cm-main hits only v2 doc commits (fdf2b9b1, 51570583, a1c01ea0) and adapter docs; v1 never replaced output on Claude Code.
findings.fix: Adapter table row for CC case C: field per tool kind (updatedToolOutput for built-ins, updatedMCPToolOutput for external MCP); LV2 must record the accepted shape per tool and assert the original bytes do NOT reach the transcript, including with a second PostToolUse hook from another plugin installed.

findings.claim: The harness runs `--plugin-dir <build> --setting-sources project` and does not pass CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR, so user-enabled plugins still load. On the owner's Mac the v1 plugin `context-mode@context-mode` is enabled at user scope. v1 and v2 then both load, with the same plugin and server name, so the tool names collide and v1 hooks (modify/deny, PreCompact, SessionStart injection) run beside v2 hooks. Every live result (routing, deny, compaction, hook timing) is contaminated.
findings.evidence: ~/.claude/settings.json:37 `"context-mode@context-mode": true`; ~/.claude/plugins/installed_plugins.json:173-177 installPath .../cache/context-mode/context-mode/1.0.168; TECH-SPEC.md:162 'The session init listed two user plugins (agents-md, telemetry) that --setting-sources project did not turn off.'
findings.archaeology: Harness is new in v2; no v1 behaviour changed.
findings.fix: Harness passes `--settings '{"enabledPlugins":{"context-mode@context-mode":false}}'` (or turns off all user plugins) and fails the run unless the stream-json init lists exactly one context-mode plugin, from <build>, and no other hooks fire for it.

findings.claim: The harness accepts the first real `claude` binary but never checks its version. On the owner's Mac two real binaries exist (2.1.283 Homebrew, 2.1.274 ~/.local/bin). Fixtures and TECH-SPEC are pinned to 2.1.283; a PATH change silently runs live checks on another version.
findings.evidence: `which -a claude`: shims, /opt/homebrew/bin/claude -> 2.1.283, /Users/mksglu/.local/bin/claude -> versions/2.1.274. TECH-SPEC.md:24 pins Claude Code 2.1.283.
findings.fix: Run `<bin> --version` and print it in report.md; fail or mark the run when it differs from the fixture version under e2e/fixtures/claude-code/<ver>.
